chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had prayed toward other than the qiblah, then the qiblah became clear to him while the time of another salat had entered. He said: He should perform that prayer before he performs this one whose time has entered, unless he fears missing the one whose time has entered.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we carry them upon the case that he had prayed facing directly away from the qiblah, for then repeating the salat is obligatory upon him whether the time remains or has expired. That is indicated by the following.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat due to invalid performance
key_terms.اسْتِدْبَارِ الْقِبْلَةِ: turning one’s back to the qiblah, i.e. facing directly away from it
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which salat is performed
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ أُخْرَى: another obligatory prayer whose time has entered
key_terms.فَوْتَ: the loss or missing of the prayer within its time

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prayed facing other than the qiblah and then discovered the correct direction?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling for one who prayed in a direction other than the qiblah and later discovered the correct direction. It indicates that the missed prayer is to be repeated before the currently due prayer, unless there is fear of missing the current prayer time. The concluding legal note explains that these reports are understood to apply to the case of having prayed in direct opposition to the qiblah, in which case repetition is obligatory whether the time remains or has passed.
